# Native packaged worker CI, source handoff

This source packet adds a public standard GitHub runner lane for native `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64` acceptance. It invokes the existing `scripts/acceptance/packaged-worker.mjs` engine without modifying the worker, Dockerfile, activity implementations or harness. Source fixtures do not establish a successful native run. Root must review, integrate, commit and push the same approved candidate, then observe both complete GitHub jobs and their exact artifacts.

The prior Mac ARM64 R4 attempt reached real TLS custody and stopped at 7.84 GiB during Temporal schema setup. That failed attempt remains failed. This source packet supplies no replacement runtime result. Native CI revision 1 remains frozen and unaccepted after root identified default Buildx endpoint portability; revision 2 adds the owned named local context without weakening the harness guard.

## Canonical command and evidence

The dedicated `packaged-worker` manifest has kind `native-packaged-worker`. Its fixed executed check identities and prerequisite definitions are consumed by the helper and matched workflow. Existing Vitest requirement discovery and report validators are unchanged.

On an authorized native Linux host, from a clean committed candidate with pinned Node 22.23.3:

```sh
ZENITH_PACKAGED_WORKER_ACCEPTANCE=1 node scripts/ci/packaged-worker-native.mjs --run --platform linux/amd64 --evidence /tmp/zenith-native-amd64/sanitized.json
ZENITH_PACKAGED_WORKER_ACCEPTANCE=1 node scripts/ci/packaged-worker-native.mjs --validate --platform linux/amd64 --evidence /tmp/zenith-native-amd64/sanitized.json
```

Use `linux/arm64` and a fresh distinct outside-source directory on a native ARM64 Linux host. The result must initially be absent. The workflow executes these same commands with a fixed matrix platform and `RUNNER_TEMP` result path. It fails on unsuccessful command exits, an absent/malformed/duplicate harness result, failed/skipped/unknown or missing fixed checks, source mismatch or incomplete cleanup. Validation does not promote a modeled fixture to observed execution. Root must match the real GitHub job outcome, commit SHA, run ID/attempt, architecture and artifact selection.

The public result contains only fixed checked scalars: commit/source/harness/wrapper/manifest/workflow digests, measured architecture and resources, job selection metadata, observed child exit, fixed check statuses, cleanup booleans, fixed limitations and a fixed failure phase. Extra payload fields are rejected. The upload names one exact sanitized JSON file, with missing-file failure. A separate `--validate-artifact` check admits only the fixed public schema before upload, including honest failed receipts; it cannot change the execution verdict. A malformed or private payload is never uploaded. Private stdout/stderr, configuration, certificates, keys and harness failure diagnostics remain outside source and are never uploaded. The wrapper removes its private scratch; the existing harness owns its separate private service credentials and diagnostics lifecycle.

## Native resources and cleanup

The helper requires actual Linux Node and Docker server architectures to match the requested platform, with `emulated:false`. It records actual free disk on the source, temporary and local Docker-root filesystems and actual host available/total RAM and Docker RAM. Admission requires 12 GiB free on each filesystem, 12 GiB total host/Docker RAM and 8 GiB available host RAM. It samples storage while the real harness runs and signals refusal below the 8 GiB reserve. It refuses remote/TLS Docker overrides and uses the current local Unix-socket context.

The public standard runner matrix is exactly `ubuntu-24.04` and `ubuntu-24.04-arm`. Hosted invocation additionally requires public repository visibility, the expected standard runner label and genuine hosted OS/architecture context. Private/internal or unknown context fails visibly. No runner purchase, larger-runner selection, emulation setup, preinstalled tool removal or unrelated cache pruning is added. Nominal hosted storage does not prove enough transient build capacity: a measured prerequisite or reserve failure remains a failure.

The parent captures unrelated Docker resources, the current builder and the original selected context metadata. It creates a fresh named owned Docker context pointing only to the already-verified Unix socket, and scopes `DOCKER_CONTEXT` to this invocation and the harness/shim. It then creates a fresh random dedicated docker-container builder against that named context. This keeps the existing harness requirement for a scalar node Endpoint intact even when a runner’s default Buildx node would expose a socket URL. Exact native owned-context metadata is rechecked before/after the build; only that unchanged context is removed after its builder/cache absence. The original environment, selected context and its original metadata must survive. It uses the pinned BuildKit image already required by the harness, `memory=4g`, a genuine native bootstrap and exact single-node container/cache metadata. Identical Buildx descriptor rows are deduplicated; divergent duplicates and multiple owned nodes refuse. It never selects its builder globally.

The transparent Docker shim delegates the original commands to real Docker. Only the exact original acceptance build command can trigger early release, after real exit zero and native loaded-image ID/platform/user/entrypoint/source-label checks. It recaptures the original BuildKit container/image IDs, exact non-URL context endpoint and sole exact writable cache volume before removing only that dedicated builder, without keep-state or global prune. Exact builder/container/cache absence and unchanged loaded image are required before an exclusive private bound marker is written. The launch reserve must recover to 12 GiB before the shim returns success, allowing private services to start. Failed builds, signals, identity mismatch or failed release cannot get a successful early admission.

The parent independently compares the release marker to its pre-build native ownership capture, exact harness run/image/source binding and final exact absences. The harness remains responsible for its labeled private services, volumes, network and acceptance image. The wrapper removes only newly pulled, fixed pinned unused dependency image references absent from its original image baseline; original resources and the selected builder must survive. Unverified ownership, an in-use image or cleanup failure fails the packet. A failed bootstrap before a complete native capture has no speculative deletion authority and must be reported with unverified cleanup.

Owned-context cleanup is separately required. The in-flight scope remains a read-only schema prerequisite before provider admission. Cloud mutation, browser approval, consumed write-grant preservation and production namespace ACL/HA acceptance remain unverified. No API/default server or live account is started.

Root-owned unrun checks are pinned Node compiler/lint and focused `tests/ci/packaged-workers.test.ts`, `tests/ci/release-gates.test.ts`, `tests/ci/gate-manifest.test.ts` and `tests/acceptance/packaged-worker.test.ts`, serialized with `--maxWorkers=1`. After independent C/root source review and exact composition integration, root owns actual GitHub native matrix execution and artifact/outcome readback. ## Primary references read 2026-10-04

[GitHub's standard hosted runner specification](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners) lists the selected public x64/ARM64 labels with 4 CPUs, 16 GB RAM and 14 GB SSD, and describes public standard usage as free. Runtime measurements still decide admission.

[Docker Buildx create](https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/buildx/create/) documents bootstrap, dedicated docker-container nodes and the separate global selection option. [Buildx ls](https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/buildx/ls/) documents supported builder-object tuple formatting. [Buildx inspect](https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/buildx/inspect/) supplies the existing harness-compatible fixed option check and has no format flag. [Buildx rm](https://docs.docker.com/reference/cli/docker/buildx/rm/) documents removal of a specified builder; this invocation does not retain its cache state.

The existing action pins were verified against their primary release pages: [checkout v4.3.1](https://github.com/actions/checkout/releases/tag/v4.3.1), [setup-node v4.4.0](https://github.com/actions/setup-node/releases/tag/v4.4.0) and [upload-artifact v4.6.2](https://github.com/actions/upload-artifact/releases/tag/v4.6.2).

## Revision 3, interrupted builder bootstrap cleanup

Revision 2 could create a builder and cache before `buildx create --bootstrap` returned nonzero or timed out, while cleanup still required a completed configuration. Revision 3 records the invocation's already-absent requested builder scope and captured owned context before awaiting bootstrap. Cleanup checks actual absence or captures the exact sole native node, bounded context endpoint, pinned BuildKit container/image, 4 GiB memory and sole cache metadata before removing that exact builder. It compares the capture to the request, original resource baseline and any completed capture. Complete matching ownership permits cleanup even when bootstrap never produced a configuration.

A partial, foreign or reconfigured capture refuses removal. Builder/cache/context cleanup flags remain false and the owned context remains available for diagnosis; the execution result stays failed with its original fixed failure phase. No raw failure text or private configuration is published. No blind builder deletion, global prune or original-context change is introduced. The normal passing path, 22 fixed check identities and manifest metadata are unchanged.

The added nonzero and timeout controls are source/ownership models, not actual failed Docker launches. Root must run the focused fixture suite and observe actual native jobs. Revision 1, revision 2 and the actual Mac/package failure receipts remain immutable.

## Revision 4, owned Linux process settlement

Revision 3 remains frozen and was rejected for direct-child termination: Docker Buildx plugins or shim children could survive a timeout and act after an absence check. Revision 4 places every outer Docker command and the existing acceptance program under a stock Linux Node supervisor created as its own session and process-group leader. The parent binds that actual live owner PID, group, session and `/proc` start time through a private IPC nonce. Only the supervisor signals its own reserved group. It keeps the leader alive through child completion, TERM, repeated empty group inventories, a second parent-side inventory and an explicit finish acknowledgement. The parent never signals a recycled numeric group.

The acceptance program and transparent shim/Docker descendants inherit that group. The private shim configuration is created exclusively only after the supervisor is reserved, and the shim checks its actual inherited group against the still-live owner before any real Docker delegation. It does not launch a detached nested supervisor. Direct-helper Docker inspection, creation and cleanup commands receive their own reserved supervisor. Bootstrap failures reach native ownership cleanup only after their subprocess group settles. A missing, mismatched or lost settlement receipt prevents builder/cache/context absence promotion and leaves those cleanup flags false. Unknown inventories and TERM-resistant groups kill only the still-owned entire group, including its leader, and return an unconfirmed failure. This supplies no positive cleanup receipt.

The existing 75-minute TERM deadline and 85-minute force boundary remain, as do 12 GiB launch reserves, the 8 GiB storage monitor, exact native image/source/BuildKit/context ownership and all 22 executed identities. The workflow removes this packet's previously chosen seven-day retention override and defers to repository policy. It still uploads only one schema-admitted sanitized file with missing-file failure. The private process facts, certificates, configuration and raw streams are never uploaded.

Six new controls use actual stock Node children on Linux: successful settlement, exact nonzero completion, a zero-exit parent leaving an inherited descendant, timeout, external cancellation and a TERM-resistant group that cannot produce a positive settlement receipt. They require Linux `/proc` and a genuine system reaper; container probes should use their own init so orphan zombies are reaped. `ZENITH_TEST_NATIVE_SUPERVISOR_REQUIRED=1` refuses a missing Linux prerequisite before hooks. The author did not run these controls. On a Mac the Linux cases remain honestly skipped unless that required flag makes the run fail. IPC/schema models are source evidence only. The external cancellation fixture exercises the same cancellation path used by the parent signal handler; a real OS-signal probe remains root-owned.

Root must run `ZENITH_TEST_NATIVE_SUPERVISOR_REQUIRED=1 npx vitest run tests/ci/packaged-workers.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` on actual Linux, controlled process probes including nonzero/timeout/OS-signal descendants and unconfirmed cleanup refusal, then a tiny positively owned Docker/Buildx settlement probe and both full native GitHub jobs against the final independently reviewed composition. Group settlement proves these known non-detaching CLI descendants have stopped; it is not account-wide process custody, an adversarial daemon protocol proof or a replacement for native Docker resource recapture. No actual subprocess settlement, Docker cleanup or native package success is claimed from author source inspection. Preserve all earlier freezes, source rejections and failed runtime receipts.
